<proposed_plan>
# TrustIntern — India-first public beta plan

## Summary

Build an account-free, real-data internship verification portal: users submit a job URL, text, company/recruiter details, or an offer document; TrustIntern returns an explainable report, a private shareable link, and a downloadable redacted PDF.

Use FastAPI + Next.js + PostgreSQL, with LangGraph coordinating bounded investigation agents. LangGraph fits the stateful, parallel, evidence-fusion workflow, but all risk decisions remain deterministic and evidence-backed—not LLM verdicts. [LangGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/)

## Architecture and data model

- Run a fast initial investigation with parallel Company, Domain, Communication, and Document agents; enforce a 90-second deadline for URL/text and 120 seconds for document submissions. Return a complete report even when a source is unavailable, clearly marking missing checks.
- Persist two strictly separate stores:
  - Canonical company intelligence: normalized company/domain entities, official/public links, source snapshots, evidence timestamps, freshness windows, and prior verification facts. This is reused for later checks of the same company.
  - Private report data: redacted indicators, final score, report PDF, and an unguessable access token. Delete raw uploads within two hours of successful processing; never reuse them for other users.
- Schedule monthly rechecks only for cached canonical entities. Re-run expired sources, preserve evidence history, and invalidate stale facts instead of silently carrying them forward.
- Use an evidence schema containing source URL, collection time, expiry, claim, observed fact, confidence, provenance, and risk contribution. Store “unavailable” as a first-class outcome.
- Generate risk scores from transparent weighted rules: payment/fee requests, identity or domain mismatches, suspiciously new/unsafe domains, contradictions, reported-scam evidence, and positive official corroboration. Use “insufficient evidence” when checks cannot confirm enough; never label someone definitively fraudulent.

## Live-source and AI decisions

- Make official/public sources the public-product baseline: Indian company and tax/business verification sources where available, company official websites, RDAP, DNS, TLS/certificate-transparency data, redirects, and public scam-report pages. RDAP is the modern standardized replacement for WHOIS, though privacy redaction means missing registrant data is not suspicious by itself. [ICANN RDAP](https://www.icann.org/rdap/)
- Add urlscan.io only as an opt-in public scan for submitted URLs; respect its per-action quota headers and show users that public scans may be visible externally. [urlscan.io API](https://urlscan.io/docs/api/)
- Do not automate Holehe, GHunt, CrossLinked, or mass Sherlock/Maigret scans in the public portal. They are privacy-sensitive, fragile against site changes/rate limits, and unsuitable as a default student safety feature. Keep advanced OSINT as a later, consent-based analyst workflow only.
- Do not make Apify Domain Enricher, SpiderFoot, Stipple, OPSWAT, or NVIDIA SVD core dependencies. Apify is valid but paid/community-maintained; SpiderFoot is useful for controlled analyst investigation, not every public request; NVIDIA SVD requires supported GPU/video infrastructure or approved service access. [Apify actor](https://apify.com/silentflow/domain-enricher/api), [NVIDIA support matrix](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/maxine/synthetic-video-detector/latest/support-matrix.html)
- Use Gemini as the primary multimodal adapter for structured PDF/image/text extraction and explanation; its API supports native PDF understanding. Verify the actual API-project quota before relying on Google AI Plus—consumer subscription access is not a production API-capacity guarantee. [Gemini document support](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/document-processing), [rate limits](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits)
- Use Groq only as a fast text-analysis fallback, behind provider-specific throttling and circuit breakers. Its limits are organization-level and vary by model. [Groq limits](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits)
- Keep a zero-AI fallback: local OCR/PDF extraction, metadata checks, URL/domain checks, and deterministic communication rules must still generate a useful report if every AI provider is unavailable. Ollama Cloud can be evaluated as an optional adapter, but is not a guaranteed free fallback. [Ollama Cloud](https://docs.ollama.com/cloud)

## Iterative implementation

1. Build foundations: repository structure, Docker development environment, typed API contracts, PostgreSQL schema, evidence ledger, source-adapter interface, report-token access, security headers, audit logging, and provider rate-limit/caching middleware.
2. Ship the core portal: URL/text submission, India-focused company/domain verification, payment/urgency/mismatch rules, explainable score, private report page, PDF export, canonical cache reuse, and graceful partial-result states.
3. Add document analysis: safe file validation, malware scanning, PDF metadata/text/OCR/layout extraction, redaction, Gemini structured extraction when available, immediate raw-file expiry, and document-specific evidence in reports.
4. Add durable investigation jobs and monthly entity refreshes: queue-backed retries, source-specific freshness policies, changed-fact timeline, recheck prioritization, and observability for timeout, source failure, cache-hit, and provider-quota rates.
5. Add advanced capabilities only after core accuracy is measured: consent-gated recruiter verification, optional media analysis, complaint/dispute correction workflow, and placement-cell analyst mode.

## Test plan and launch criteria

- Unit-test normalizers, redaction, evidence deduplication, freshness, scoring, token access, and every timeout/rate-limit/fallback path.
- Integration-test adapters with recorded fixtures and live smoke tests that never exceed provider quotas.
- Build a consented, manually labeled Indian internship corpus with genuine, suspicious, and inconclusive cases; evaluate false positives, false negatives, evidence quality, report clarity, and median completion time before changing score weights.
- Run end-to-end tests for cache reuse: a second check of the same company must reuse still-fresh public facts while independently analyzing the new user submission.
- Launch as a capacity-limited public beta with request throttles, visible privacy terms, a report-correction channel, and clear “decision support, not legal proof” wording. Free hosting is suitable for a public beta, not an uptime-guaranteed production service; for example, Render explicitly warns against production use of free instances and its free Postgres expires after 30 days. [Render free-tier limits](https://render.com/docs/free)

## Assumptions

- India is the first supported jurisdiction.
- No user accounts; private report links and downloadable PDFs provide revisiting/sharing.
- Raw user uploads are never part of the reusable company-intelligence cache.
- “Perfect” detection is not a valid claim; TrustIntern ships as transparent, evidence-led safety assistance with measurable accuracy and continuous calibration.
</proposed_plan>
